content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato fries are batata sticks that are deep‑fried or baked until crisp. They have a natural sweetness, golden color, and crunchy texture. Frequently served as a side or snack in fast‑food and restaurant menus.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes contain more beta‑carotene than regular potatoes, giving the fries a bright orange hue.
They are often paired with a variety of sauces: garlic, chili, yogurt‑based, or honey‑mustard.
Compared to regular potatoes, sweet potatoes have a lower glycemic index, though they should still be eaten in moderation.
In some countries sweet potato fries are marketed as a healthier alternative to traditional fries.
Sweet potatoes are cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions but have adapted to temperate climates as well.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts antioxidant protection and immune function.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytochemicals in sweet potatoes combat free radicals, reducing the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds significant fat, so portion control is important.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature cooking can produce acrylamide, a potential toxin; lower temperatures or baking are safer.

items.title: Sweet potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to sweet potatoes; discontinue use if symptoms appear.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve sweet potato fries hot, seasoned with salt, spices, or herbs. They can be enjoyed as a snack, in burgers, alongside salads, or as a side dish to meats. For a healthier option, bake the sticks with a light coating of oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fries in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or air‑fryer to restore crispness.
